chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Jahm ibn Abi Jahm, who said:

I saw Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Ja'far عليه السلام, and he had performed a sajdah after the three rak'ahs of Maghrib. So I said to him: May I be your ransom, I saw you perform sajdah after the three. He said: You saw me? I said: Yes. He said: Then do not leave it, for du'a in it is answered.

The proper way regarding this narration is that we carry it upon a kind of recommendation, and the first one upon permissibility. And his statement in the first report, 'None of my forefathers would perform sajdah except after the seventh,' is to inform that they did not choose to do it, or that they did not perform it as an obligation, even if they did perform it by way of merit.

key_terms.الثَّلَاثِ الرَّكَعَاتِ: the three rak'ahs of the Maghrib prayer

ai.seo_question: Is the sajdah of shukr between the Maghrib obligation and its nawafil recommended in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report describes Imam Mūsā ibn Ja'far عليه السلام performing a sajdah after the three rak'ahs of Maghrib and stating that du'a in it is answered. The accompanying legal explanation reconciles this with another report by understanding this sajdah as recommended rather than obligatory, while the other report indicates permissibility or non-preference rather than prohibition.
